newsitem.title: USA: Merrill sees Fed tightening in H2 1997.
newsitem.headline: Merrill sees Fed tightening in H2 1997.

text.p: Merrill Lynch and Co Inc gave an upbeat forecast for the U.S. economy in 1997 on Tuesday and expected the Federal Reserve to tighten credit in the second half of next year.
Merrill's team of senior researchers, led by chief economist Donald Straszheim, saw the Fed keeping the "federal funds rate unchanged at 5.25 percent until the second half, then tighten."
The Fed held its last meeting of 1996 on Tuesday, leaving the funds rate and the 5.0-percent discount rate unchanged. The Fed last moved and lowered both rates on February 1.
Merrill analysts, in their forecasts, expected the U.S. Gross Domestic Product to grow by 2.0 percent next year and the Consumer Price Index to rise by 2.8 percent.
The 30-year Treasury bond yield should trade in a 6.0- to 7.0-percent range in 1997, while the dollar should end the year at "around 120 yen and 1.70 marks," they also said.
"Economic expansions in the United States typically don't die of old age. They die of disease -- one imbalance or another," Straszheim told a press briefing.
